concept.name: LLM Fine-Tuning & LoRA

relationships.description: Connects LLM Fine-Tuning & LoRA to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) freezes a pretrained LLM's weights and trains tiny rank-decomposed adapter matrices, cutting fine-tuning VRAM by 3–10x while preserving base capabilities.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use LoRA/QLoRA when you need consistent domain formatting, tone, or latency-critical distillation into smaller models—not to inject rapidly changing facts that belong in RAG.

concept.whyItMatters: Full fine-tuning of a 70B-parameter model requires >1 TB of GPU memory for weights, gradients, and AdamW optimizer states, making iteration prohibitively expensive and risking catastrophic forgetting. LoRA updates <1% of parameters via low-rank matrices (`B * A`), fitting 70B QLoRA training onto a single 48–80 GB GPU and letting serving engines like vLLM hot-swap dozens of task adapters over one shared base model.
whenToUse: Teaching strict, complex output schemas, domain-specific DSLs, or consistent brand/clinical tone where few-shot prompting fails or consumes too many input tokens.
Distilling a frontier model's reasoning or classification behavior (generated via synthetic/curated traces) into an 8B–14B model to cut inference latency and cost by 5–15x.
Multi-tenant serving where one frozen base model hosts hundreds of customer- or task-specific adapters with near-zero memory overhead per tenant.
whenNotToUse: Injecting fresh, mutable knowledge (product catalogs, policies, daily news)—fine-tuning is slow to update and still hallucinates facts; use RAG instead.
When you have fewer than ~200–500 clean, diverse training examples or haven't first established a strong prompt + RAG baseline.
Tasks requiring broad new reasoning capabilities absent from the base model family without massive continual pretraining.
keyPoints: LoRA freezes `W_0` (dimension `d x k`) and learns `ΔW = (alpha / r) * B * A`, where `A` is `r x k`, `B` is `d x r`, and rank `r` is typically 8–64.
Applying LoRA to all linear layers (`q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `o_proj`, plus MLP `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`) consistently outperforms attention-only adaptation.
QLoRA quantizes the frozen base weights to 4-bit NormalFloat (`NF4`) with double quantization and paged optimizers, fitting a 70B model into ~48 GB VRAM.
Data quality dominates dataset size: 1,000–5,000 deduplicated, human-verified examples routinely beat 100,000 noisy scraped rows.
At inference, adapters can either be merged into `W_0` (`W_0 + ΔW`) for zero latency overhead or served dynamically via multi-LoRA kernels (Punica/S-LoRA in vLLM).

examples.title: Distilling Frontier SQL Generation to Llama-3.1-8B
examples.scenario: A BI SaaS spent $18k/month calling a frontier API with a 4,500-token few-shot prompt to generate ClickHouse SQL. They curated 3,200 validated `(schema, question, sql)` pairs and trained a QLoRA adapter (`r=32, alpha=64`) on `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` using `trl.SFTTrainer`.
examples.outcome: Execution accuracy matched the frontier baseline at 93.1% while dropping prompt length by 75% and p95 latency from 2.4s to 340 ms on a single L40S GPU.

examples.title: Multi-Tenant Compliance Redaction in vLLM
examples.scenario: An enterprise platform needed 12 region-specific PII/PHI redaction policies without spinning up 12 separate 14B model deployments.
examples.outcome: They trained 12 `safetensors` LoRA adapters (~85 MB each) against one `Qwen2.5-14B` base and served them via vLLM `--enable-lora`, holding GPU memory under 32 GB with <4% throughput overhead.

tradeOffs.pro: Higher rank (`r=32–64`) increases adapter capacity for complex multi-task or code/DSL distributions.
tradeOffs.con: Increases adapter checkpoint size, VRAM for activations, and overfitting risk on small (<1k row) datasets.

tradeOffs.pro: QLoRA slashes base model VRAM by ~70% (e.g., 70B in ~48 GB vs ~140 GB), enabling training on single-GPU nodes.
tradeOffs.con: Dequantization during forward/backward passes slows training throughput by ~20–35% compared to native BF16.

tradeOffs.factor: Merged Weights vs. Dynamic Multi-LoRA Serving
tradeOffs.pro: Merging `W_0 + (alpha/r)BA` eliminates runtime adapter overhead and supports standard TensorRT-LLM/FP8 quantization.
tradeOffs.con: Loses the ability to share one base model across multiple tenants or A/B test adapters on the same GPU pool.

failureModes.name: Catastrophic Forgetting / Narrow Overfitting
failureModes.description: Training for too many epochs (e.g., 8–10) on a narrow JSON task destroys general instruction following and refusal behavior.
failureModes.mitigation: Train for 1–3 epochs, mix in 10–20% general instruction replay data, and monitor held-out general benchmarks alongside task evals.

failureModes.name: Chat Template & EOS Token Mismatch
failureModes.description: Training data omits the base model's exact special tokens (`<|eot_id|>`, `<|im_end|>`), causing the fine-tuned model to ramble endlessly at inference.
failureModes.mitigation: Always apply `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` identically in training and serving, and verify loss masking (`DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM`) only trains on assistant turns.

failureModes.name: Rank/Alpha Scaling Instability
failureModes.description: Changing `r` without adjusting `lora_alpha` or learning rate causes gradient spikes or underfitting.
failureModes.mitigation: Keep `lora_alpha = 2 * r` (or use `rsLoRA` scaling `alpha / sqrt(r)` for high ranks) and sweep learning rates in `1e-4` to `3e-4`.

failureModes.name: Loss Computed on Prompt Tokens
failureModes.description: Standard causal LM training computes cross-entropy loss over the entire system prompt and user query, wasting capacity memorizing inputs.
failureModes.mitigation: Mask prompt tokens with `-100` in labels so gradients flow exclusively from target assistant completions.

commonMistakes: Fine-tuning to memorize changing facts instead of pairing a base/LoRA model with RAG.
Training on unfiltered synthetic outputs without deduplication or execution verification, amplifying base model hallucinations.
Adapting only `q_proj` and `v_proj` when targeting complex reasoning or formatting—missing MLP layers leaves accuracy on the table.
Skipping a baseline prompt-engineered eval first, making it impossible to prove fine-tuning actually helped.
Forgetting to match quantization precision (`bitsandbytes` NF4 vs FP8/AWQ) between merged weights and the inference engine.

sections.content:
## The idea

Pretrained LLMs are over-parameterized for any single downstream task: weight updates during fine-tuning empirically have a **low intrinsic rank**. Instead of updating a full `d x k` weight matrix `W_0` (e.g., `4096 x 4096` = 16.7M parameters), **LoRA** freezes `W_0` and injects a parallel trainable bypass:

`h = W_0 * x + (alpha / r) * B * A * x`

Here `A` (`r x k`, initialized with Gaussian noise) projects down to rank `r` (e.g., `16`), and `B` (`d x r`, initialized to zeros) projects back up to `d`. At step 0, `B * A = 0`, so the model starts at the exact pretrained behavior. During training, optimizer states (AdamW `m` and `v`, which normally consume 2x–4x model weight memory) are stored **only for `A` and `B`**—shrinking trainable parameters to ~0.1%–1% of the model.

## Concrete walkthrough

Walk through fine-tuning **Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct** on 2,500 support-ticket triage examples using `peft` + `trl` on a single 24 GB RTX 4090 / A10G:

1. **Prepare & Mask Data**: Format each row with `tokenizer.apply_chat_template`, split 90/10 train/eval, and use `DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM` so loss is masked (`-100`) on system/user tokens.
2. **Load Quantized Base (QLoRA)**: Load the base model in 4-bit `NF4` (`bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True`, `bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16`). Base weights occupy ~5.5 GB VRAM.
3. **Attach LoRA Config**: Configure `LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"])`. Trainable params: ~40M (~0.5% of 7.6B).
4. **Train (`SFTTrainer`)**: Run 2 epochs with `paged_adamw_8bit`, `lr=2e-4`, cosine schedule with 5% warmup, effective batch size 16 (micro-batch 2 x grad-accum 8), and `bf16=True`. Peak VRAM sits around ~16 GB; run finishes in ~25 minutes.
5. **Evaluate & Export**: Run the held-out eval harness against the saved `adapter_model.safetensors` (~160 MB). Either load dynamically in `vLLM` or call `merge_and_unload()` to export a standalone merged model.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Targeting modules, rank selection, and DPO
sections.content:
## Targeting modules, rank selection, and DPO

Three tuning levers determine whether a LoRA run hits production quality:

- **Target Modules**: Always adapt both attention (`q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj`) and MLP projections (`gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj`). For 7B–70B models, MLP layers store most factual/stylistic associations and carry the largest accuracy gains.
- **Rank `r` & Learning Rate**: Start with `r=16, lora_alpha=32`. Use `r=8` for narrow classification/formatting, and `r=32–64` for code generation or multilingual adaptation. Because `alpha/r` acts as a multiplier on the update, keeping `alpha = 2 * r` lets you change `r` without wildly retuning `lr` (`1e-4` to `2e-4`).
- **SFT + DPO Alignment**: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) teaches format and domain vocabulary, but **Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)** on `(prompt, chosen, rejected)` pairs using a LoRA adapter (`beta=0.1`, `lr=5e-6`) sharply reduces subtle policy violations, verbosity, and hallucinated edge cases.

## Fine-tuning approaches compared

| Method | Trainable Params | 70B VRAM (Training) | Training Speed | Best Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Full Fine-Tuning (BF16)** | 100% (70B) | ~1,120 GB (14x H100) | Baseline | Continual pretraining on 10B+ domain tokens |
| **LoRA (BF16)** | ~0.5% (350M) | ~160 GB (2x H100) | 1.3x faster | High-throughput domain tuning when multi-GPU is available |
| **QLoRA (4-bit NF4)** | ~0.5% (350M) | ~48 GB (1x A6000/A100) | 0.7–0.8x (dequant overhead) | Cost-effective tuning of 14B–70B models on 1 GPU |
| **Prompt / Prefix Tuning** | <0.05% | ~140 GB (frozen BF16) | Fast | Legacy; largely superseded by LoRA + prompt caching |
| **Prompting + Few-Shot + RAG** | 0% | 0 (API / inference only) | Instant iteration | Rapid prototyping, dynamic knowledge, <500 examples |

## Failure modes

1. **Quantization-Induced Accuracy Drop After Merge**: Merging a 4-bit QLoRA adapter back into a 4-bit quantized model directly introduces rounding error. *Fix*: Dequantize the base model to BF16/FP16 first, merge the LoRA weights (`merge_and_unload()`), and then re-quantize (AWQ/FP8) with calibration data.
2. **Severe Overfitting on Small Datasets**: Eval loss starts rising after epoch 1.5 while train loss approaches 0.1. *Fix*: Lower epochs to 1–2, increase `lora_dropout` to `0.05–0.1`, add weight decay (`0.01`), or reduce rank `r`.
3. **Data Leakage Between Train and Eval**: Near-duplicate synthetic prompts appear in both splits, inflating eval scores. *Fix*: Run MinHash/embedding deduplication (>0.85 similarity) before splitting.
4. **OOM During Long-Context Training**: Sequence length `4096+` blows up activation memory even with QLoRA. *Fix*: Enable `gradient_checkpointing=True`, FlashAttention-2 (`attn_implementation="flash_attention_2"`), and pack short sequences with `packing=True`.

## Data curation and distillation workflow

In practice, 80% of LoRA engineering is data curation:

- **Rejection Sampling**: Generate 4–8 candidate responses per prompt from a strong teacher model, filter strictly with deterministic validators (unit tests, JSON schema, SQL execution, or reward model), and keep only verified winners.
- **Length & Format Hygiene**: Strip conversational filler (*"Sure, here is..."*) from training targets if you want terse production outputs; models mimic the exact whitespace and verbosity of training completions.
- **Mix General Replay**: Include 10–15% general instruction-following examples (e.g., Magpie/Tulu subsets) so the adapted model retains multi-turn coherence and safety boundaries.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Verify prompt engineering + RAG cannot already hit the target accuracy/latency SLA before training.
- [ ] Curate 1,000–5,000 deduplicated examples formatted with the exact serving `apply_chat_template`.
- [ ] Mask prompt tokens (`-100`) so cross-entropy loss applies only to assistant completions.
- [ ] Target all attention + MLP linear layers with `r=16, lora_alpha=32` (or `r=32, alpha=64`) and `gradient_checkpointing=True`.
- [ ] Evaluate checkpoints at every 0.5 epoch on both the task golden set and a general capability/safety slice.
- [ ] Merge into BF16 before re-quantizing to FP8/AWQ, or serve raw `safetensors` adapters via vLLM multi-LoRA.

simulation.title: Interactive Simulation: Llm Fine Tuning Lora

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) freezes a pretrained LLM's weights and trains tiny rank-decomposed adapter matrices, cutting fine-tuning VRAM by 3–10x while preserving base capabilities.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: LoRA Adapters applies the primary invariant and coordinates with vLLM / Merged Serving.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, vLLM / Merged Serving experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Train for 1–3 epochs, mix in 10–20% general instruction replay data, and monitor held-out general benchmarks alongside task evals.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Use LoRA/QLoRA when you need consistent domain formatting, tone, or latency-critical distillation into smaller models—not to inject rapidly changing facts that belong in RAG.
Avoid trap: Fine-tuning to memorize changing facts instead of pairing a base/LoRA model with RAG.
Avoid trap: Training on unfiltered synthetic outputs without deduplication or execution verification, amplifying base model hallucinations.
When to reach for it: Teaching strict, complex output schemas, domain-specific DSLs, or consistent brand/clinical tone where few-shot prompting fails or consumes too many input tokens.
When to reach for it: Distilling a frontier model's reasoning or classification behavior (generated via synthetic/curated traces) into an 8B–14B model to cut inference latency and cost by 5–15x.

putItTogether.title: Putting Llm Fine Tuning Lora Together
putItTogether.summary: Use LoRA/QLoRA when you need consistent domain formatting, tone, or latency-critical distillation into smaller models—not to inject rapidly changing facts that belong in RAG.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Llm Fine Tuning Lora before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Execution accuracy matched the frontier baseline at 93.1% while dropping prompt length by 75% and p95 latency from 2.4s to 340 ms on a single L40S GPU.
